description: A dependency-free Python push bus that joins named inputs, invokes ordinary functions and emits values through output templates.
scope_audience: The target is an application developer needing in-process event routing with join keys, optional inputs, buffering, consume behavior, grace timers, provenance and statistics. It is explicitly not a persistent queue or async runtime.

creativity.reason: Named regex joins, per-input provenance and grace-bounded emission form an interesting compact composition; competing libraries were not compared, so novelty is open.

current_usefulness.reason: The implementation exposes a concrete PushBus API and inspected tests cover joins, optional values, provenance, timers and error isolation; none were run here.

expected_usefulness.reason: If completed at its written scope, it can remove custom buffering/join logic from event-driven applications while retaining plain Python callbacks; threading remains caller-owned.

impl_progress.reason: The code contains per-key buffers, locking, timers, output mapping and statistics; focused tests exercise many contract cases, with concurrency and runtime results not independently verified.

presentability.reason: README gives the package boundary and test command and links both the contract plan and implementation; no installation or caller example was run.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The library and focused contract tests are present at its closed milestone; external threading/asynchrony and persistence are non-goals.

contribution: A caller-facing push-routing contract centered on named inputs and ordinary callbacks, with state behavior such as optional joins, provenance and bounded grace made explicit. Its implementation is more than a plan, but no comparative library search establishes uniqueness.
